newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African tourism body in chaos, new chief says.
newsitem.headline: S.African tourism body in chaos, new chief says.

text.p: The para-statal body charged with promoting tourism to South Africa is in chaos and four managers are being probed for fraud or corruption, Michael Farr, the body's new chief executive officer, said on Wednesday.

Farr, appointed earlier this year to head a management shake-up of Satour, told a parliamentary committee that Deputy President Thabo Mbeki had authorised additional help for the investigation into irregularities at Satour's head office and it office in Paris.
"The complication to the process (of transformation) is the state of chaos of the organisation," Farr said.

"It is difficult to understand how it could have malfunctioned as long as it has malfunctioned, especially when the auditor-general had in the past three years brought to the attention of parliament the fact that this is an organisation which lacks inernal controls or financial management systems...
"In any organisation characterised by such a lack of control, it is inevitable that you are going to find irregularities," he said.
Farr declined to name any of the people being investigated, but said the irregularities included the manipulation of tender procedures to favour certain companies.
Citing an example of past mismanagement, he said Satour six years ago signed a 25-year lease on office space in Wimbledon, London, at 10 pounds (750 rand) a square meter above market rates.
